ru: Подними́тесь на ли́фте на пя́тый эта́ж.
en_alt: Go up in the lift to the fifth floor.
note: Adds the literal 'go up in the lift' rendering of подняться на лифте alongside the idiomatic 'take the lift'.

en_alt: We waited a long time for the lift.
note: More usual English word order for the same sentence.
Here ли́чность means 'identity', which the headword gloss 'personality' does not cover; the English is right, so the gloss is probably the half that needs widening.

en: He is a very striking personality.
en_alt: He is a very bright personality.
He is a very colourful character.
note: 'A bright personality' is not what an English speaker says for я́ркая ли́чность; 'striking' keeps it natural.

ru: Они́ плыву́т на ло́дке по реке́.
en: They are sailing along the river in a boat.
en_alt: They are going along the river in a boat.
They are sailing a boat along the river.
note: 'Sailing a boat' makes the boat a direct object and implies a sailing boat; на ло́дке is 'in a boat'.

en_alt: There is a small boat on the shore.
note: Existential rendering is the more usual English for На берегу́ стои́т…

en: It is more convenient to eat soup with wooden spoons.
en_alt: Soup is more convenient to eat with wooden spoons.
note: 'Soup is more convenient to eat with…' is translationese; the impersonal 'it is more convenient to eat soup' is the natural English of удо́бнее есть.

en_alt: Add two spoonfuls of sugar.
note: 'Spoonfuls' is the usual English measure word here; both readings should be accepted.

en_alt: She is tired of the constant lies.
note: 'Lies' is the more literal rendering of лжи; 'lying' is equally valid.

ru: Они́ стоя́ли плечо́м к плечу́, ло́ктем к ло́ктю.

note: «облокоти́ться на ло́коть» is tautological — облокоти́ться already means to lean on one's elbow; a native would say «Он опёрся на ло́коть» or «Он облокоти́лся о стол».

en_alt: Give me this spade.
note: э́ту is 'this'; the demonstrative should be accepted either way.

ru: На коню́шне ве́чером задаю́т лошадя́м се́но.
en_alt: In the evening they give the horses hay in the stable.
note: Equally valid ordering of the two adverbials.

ru: Они́ подъе́хали к до́му на лошадя́х.
en_alt: They rode up to the house on horseback.
note: 'On horseback' is the idiomatic English for на лошадя́х.

ru: Ста́рый ковбо́й всю жизнь рабо́тал с лошадьми́.

en_alt: A horse is grazing in the field.
note: Russian present covers both English presents; both should be accepted.

en_alt: There are a lot of bright flowers in the meadow.
note: 'A lot of' is the more literal rendering of мно́го.

en_alt: Onions make your eyes water.
note: English usually pluralises 'onions' in this generic statement.

en_alt: She is cutting the onion on the board.
note: Definite article is at least as natural here; Russian marks neither.

en_alt: The moon is bright today.
note: Сего́дня is literally 'today'; both renderings are fine.

en_alt: The first ray of the sun woke me.
note: Article and the bare 'woke me' are equally valid.

en: The room was full of rays of sunlight.
en_alt: The room was full of sunbeams.
The room was full of sun rays.
note: 'Sun rays' is not idiomatic English; 'rays of sunlight' keeps the headword luch visible where 'sunbeams' would hide it.

en_alt: In winter it is hard here without skis.
note: Equally valid ordering of the adverbials.

ru: Он ката́ется на лы́жах в гора́х.
en_alt: He goes skiing in the mountains.
note: 'Goes skiing' tracks ката́ется на лы́жах more closely than the bare verb 'skis'.

ru: Кни́гу написа́л люби́тель, а не учёный.
en_alt: An amateur wrote the book, not a scholar.
note: Active rendering matches the Russian word order; the passive is also fine.
Here люби́тель is 'lover/enthusiast', a sense the headword gloss 'amateur' does not cover; the English is right, so the gloss is likely the half to widen.
Same gloss gap as the previous sentence: люби́телей is 'lovers/enthusiasts', not 'amateurs'; the gloss 'amateur' looks too narrow.

ru: Он гото́в на всё ра́ди любви́.
en_alt: He is ready for anything for the sake of love.
note: More literal rendering of гото́в на всё ра́ди.

en_alt: She spoke quietly about love.
note: More usual English adverb placement.

ru: Любопы́тство привело́ его́ в стра́нный дом.
en_alt: Curiosity led him into a strange house.
note: в + accusative is 'into', and the indefinite article is at least as natural.

ru: Она́ смотре́ла на меня́ с любопы́тством.

note: A car falls into a manhole, not a 'hatch', so the English is right but needs a sense the headword gloss 'hatch' does not carry.

en_alt: There is a round table under the chandelier.
note: Existential rendering is equally natural for Под лю́строй стои́т…

ru: В суббо́ту она́ лю́бит ходи́ть по магази́нам без спе́шки.
en: On Saturday she likes to go round the shops without rushing.
en_alt: On Saturday she likes to wander round the shops without hurrying.
On Saturday she likes to go round the shops unhurriedly.
note: 'Wander' and 'hurrying' add colour the Russian does not have; ходи́ть по магази́нам без спе́шки is 'go round the shops without rushing'.

ru: Я иду́ в магази́н за хле́бом.
В сосе́дних магази́нах молоко́ сто́ит по-ра́зному.
en_alt: Milk costs different amounts in the neighbouring shops.
note: Equally valid English ordering.

en_alt: In summer he goes around in T-shirts.
note: 'Goes around' is the commoner variant of 'goes about'.

en_alt: There was no pasta left on the plate.
note: The Russian past не оста́лось supports the past reading too.

ru: Тре́нер разреши́л ма́льчикам поигра́ть ещё полчаса́.

en_alt: The teacher told the lad off.
note: Colloquial equivalent of сде́лать замеча́ние, matching the colloquial мальчи́шка.

en_alt: It was fun at the stag do.
note: More literal rendering of the impersonal На мальчи́шнике бы́ло ве́село.

en_alt: He came back late from the stag do.
note: More usual English adverb placement.

ru: Мы пошли́ к ма́ме в го́сти.

en_alt: Mum, I have come home!
note: Literal rendering of пришла́ домо́й alongside the idiomatic 'I'm home'.

en: I promise my mum I will help.
en_alt: I promise my mum that I will help.
I promise mum I will help.
note: 'Promise someone to help' is not idiomatic English; the that-clause is how this is said.

en: The stamp was not enough for the letter.
en_alt: There was not enough on the stamp for the letter.
note: 'Not enough on the stamp' invents a postage value the Russian never mentions; ма́рки не хвати́ло is simply that the stamp did not suffice.

ru: Она́ верну́лась из Маро́кко с сувени́рами.

en_alt: In the summer we will go to Morocco.
note: Uncontracted form and article variant should both be accepted.

en_alt: The bus runs on a new route.
note: 'Runs on a route' is the idiomatic English for a bus service.

ru: Де́ти пришли́ на пра́здник в ма́сках.
На маскара́д все пришли́ в костю́мах.
Она́ танцева́ла на маскара́де всю ночь.

en_alt: There are lots of black olives in the salad.
note: Matches the headword gloss 'black olive'; the shorter 'olives' is also fine.

ru: На пло́щади собрала́сь огро́мная ма́сса люде́й.

en: He has masses of free time.
en_alt: He has loads of free time.
He has a huge amount of free time.
note: 'A mass of free time' is not English; ма́сса in this quantifier sense is 'masses/loads of'.

en: After work she gives a massage.
en_alt: After work she does a massage.
note: 'Does a massage' is not idiomatic; де́лать масса́ж of the practitioner is 'give a massage'.
«Она́ рабо́тает на масса́же» is loose colloquial Russian (a native would say «рабо́тает масса́жисткой»), and the English adds 'parlour', which the Russian does not say.

ru: Он пошёл в мастерску́ю за инструме́нтом.

en_alt: The workshop is located in the courtyard.
note: More literal rendering of нахо́дится.

ru: Нам не хвата́ет материа́ла для кры́ши.
en_alt: We do not have enough material for the roof.
note: не хвата́ет is literally 'there is not enough'; 'we lack' is also fine.

ru: Учи́тель объясни́л но́вый материа́л на уро́ке.

en_alt: My mother works in a school.
note: Preposition and article vary freely here in English.

en_alt: The car needs washing.
note: Equally natural English for на́до помы́ть.

en_alt: He is driving the car.
note: Russian present covers both English presents.
